desc: Prove CJ's Bluetooth acceptance test: an OBEX object-push file transfer between the M1 host (controller F8:4D:89:6C:92:CB) and the M4, in either direction. Runs on the headless WiFi/BT RAM root so it is INDEPENDENT of the dirty-SD gate (215/216) and touches no storage. Exact members, all hash-pinned and two-build-identical where built here: IMAGE=Image 43e1a7d4656b7cd692b7217fdccb77bf68c96a28b79e8579dad1d73ee369b8e5 (Linux 7.1.3-g4f2429104009, pcie-apple+macsmc+brcmfmac+hci_bcm4377 builtin); DTB t6040-j614s-dcuart-wifi-cpufreq.dtb 7fea8942aadb47ed83915f95e210c489d64264ca1420913a13635ca48d702cfa; initramfs initramfs-alpine-wifi-obex.v3build1.cpio.gz 6de5abfea4ca552c608667031f8a6f92da2dd5894823d22c9b802910d9005c41 (T6040_OBEX=1, two clean byte-identical builds). Procedure: tethered chainload at maxcpus=1, wait for WiFi+sshd, then over ssh run 't6040-bt-obex receive' and confirm hci0 UP, org.bluez.obex PRESENT on the session bus, adapter discoverable, and the OPP UUID advertised. Then the transfer: M1->M4 is the preferred direction because it needs no macOS Sharing system-setting change (macOS sends outbound via Bluetooth File Exchange); M4->M1 additionally requires Bluetooth Sharing enabled on the Mac, which is CJ's to enable. Pass = a file arrives with a matching SHA-256 in either direction. Read-only w.r.t. all storage; no SMC/SPMI/PMU/charger/NVRAM/firmware write; rfkill unblock of the BT soft-block only.
